## Current session integration — 8 September 2026

**Bootstrap accessibility fixes pushed to the existing [PR #30920](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/30920)**, head `66074c6928278faca86ae8b2952c17f409cbea51`, still **DRAFT**. No new PR, force-push, merge or deployment. Original #29918 acceptance remains **0/3 complete all-provider cycles**.

### Newly delivered three-file increment

The actual Bootstrap recovery screen now uses the existing readable help-text token, the canonical form Input's existing filled keyboard-focus treatment, and the established Start-over action size with a 44px coarse-pointer target. No submission, reset, identity or lifecycle handler changed. The shared Input form variant intentionally benefits other callers too; it does not alter values, focus order or layout dimensions. The design-system's global ring policy remains unchanged.

Four permanent full-app browser tests reproduce the original contrast/focus failures and check the rendered correction: help/link contrast at least 4.5:1 before/after invalid-token feedback, real Tab/focus-visible paint changes, no horizontal overflow, and actual coarse-pointer input/Start-over geometry. An intermediate run exposed the 16px coarse-pointer Start-over target; it was corrected without weakening assertions. These tests use isolated HTTP collaborators, not real provider exchanges.

### Qualification and its limits

- Fresh `origin/develop`: `357084b3092efb39f95807bcd459baadcc39f095`, already an ancestor. Whole-branch content fingerprint **139 paths**, `6e233bb3c1108182a85f94b9d1507d0a875662ed4aaa0e971f6b7db4135be5c5`, unchanged through the final tests, commit and push. Node 24.15.0 / Bun 1.3.14; no dependency changes.
- Frozen-source root `bun run verify`: **373/373 tasks**, exit 0, including UI typecheck/lint and final repository audits. Changed-file Biome and diff checks pass; the 10,153-byte increment secret scan found no leaks.
- Targeted UI tests: **36/36**, exit 0. The preceding concurrent run had 35 passes and one 10-second beforeEach timeout. The unchanged command passed without concurrent builds in 5.69 seconds; the failed log is preserved, and neither timeouts nor assertions were relaxed. This supports a preparation-time timeout, not a claim that the whole suite is universally non-flaky.
- Independent scoped Bugbot substitute: no new confirmed finding in the three-file delta; independently executed **4/4 browser tests** on the final v16 renderer. Review covers the current delta and representative Input consumers, not a new exhaustive review of all 139 branch paths or a security approval.
- Canonical `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app`: **222/222 checks**, exit 0, strict gates retained. Among 216 view/viewport entries: 199 good, 17 needs-eyeball, zero broken/needs-work. Packaged OCR: 204 verified, 12 needs-eyeball, zero broken/new regressions. All 21 affected Bootstrap after-captures were individually inspected, plus eight broader desktop/phone captures. This is not a claim that all 216 images or every hidden/shared form/theme received manual inspection.
- Before renderer is clean `c9112903`, build `73f6778ee6ea73741763762cce980c57ba603bee607a820fbeb502c623e5bdd8`. After is the reviewed three-file delta atop that commit, renderer `9a6a1e580af9f0621dbfd5b042ae8f5626574ae7c02f3dc0ac541b162c5c7f30`, built 18:34:25 UTC. The truthful pre-commit manifest is preserved; it is not mislabeled an installed or served staging build of the new SHA.

Exact-head hosted [PR Static Smoke 34265165075](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/34265165075): **completed / success**, read at 2026-09-08T21:52:46.865Z.

The preceding `c9112903` CI run [34260137457](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/34260137457) completed successfully. Its 3,911-test expanded sweep, 19 app-bootstrap checks and scoped persistence review remain historical qualification of that named source, not newly executed whole-PR tests for this increment.

The published bundle contains 35 original before/after PNGs, five full silent MP4s, console/network records and the source/media/OCR manifest. All 42 remote assets were verified against local SHA256 and byte size (2,196,105 bytes). Desktop 1280×900, narrow fine-pointer 390×844 and an additional coarse-pointer 390×844 after-context are covered. This is browser emulation, not installed mobile or live authentication. Expected fixture 401/blocked notification errors remain in the logs. Real backend/domain receipts are N/A for this isolated capture, not silently treated as successful backend evidence.

### Remaining before Ready and original product acceptance

Supplemental shared-consumer check, 8 September 18:57 UTC: the real built Pairing gate was inspected in four isolated contexts (desktop/coarse pointer × OS dark/light preference). All eight rest/focus PNGs were opened. The field visibly changes background/border under keyboard focus without changing its box; its height is 48px, and no page overflow or pageerror was observed. No code was entered/submitted and no non-GET request occurred; one expected fixture-401 console entry remains per context. The application actually renders its single supported dark theme under both OS preferences (`persistence.ts` normalizes legacy modes to dark), so this is not a fabricated light-app certification. An initial diagnostic sampled the unfocused color during its transition and failed; waiting for the real transition to settle and navigating with Tab/Shift+Tab passed without any source change. These supplemental captures/logs remain local and do not replace missing complete-flow/device evidence or the published Bootstrap bundle.

Supplemental storage-availability recovery: the real full-app renderer now has reviewed evidence of **unavailable → Retry/Checking → unauthenticated Pairing**, in desktop 1280×900 and narrow 390×844 desktop-RPC browser contexts. Both retain `/chat` and the selected remote fixture. Native storage reads and normal startup collaborators are simulated; no credential is supplied or submitted. This proves the local integration can resume startup after availability returns, **not** successful account authentication, real OS vault recovery, installed desktop/mobile qualification, or a live-provider cycle.

All six original PNGs and selected OCR outputs were inspected. Two complete silent MP4s (5.92s and 6.00s) were reviewed through chronological 2fps contact sheets, not frame-by-frame playback. Each includes a sampled black transition before stable Pairing; no no-flash/performance clearance is claimed. OCR misses inverse action labels, checked against originals. No pageerror, page overflow, non-GET HTTP request, blocked request or unknown RPC method occurred in the successful captures; seven expected redacted storage-unavailable console errors remain per context. Native wake/tray/auth-status calls use explicit inert collaborators, so this is not a claim that normal app startup has no native effects. Earlier fixture failures are preserved and documented in the manifest; no product source or assertion was weakened.

The whole-candidate independent security review still has **no final verdict** after the review tool could not complete. Earlier scoped reviews and green CI do not replace it. Successful **authenticated** recovery, remaining installed-platform/process-spanning qualification, and the complete applicable shared-consumer evidence remain incomplete. The historical Storybook failures were reproduced on clean develop at the prior snapshot; that comparison is not a blanket waiver for current changes. Do not mark Ready from these scoped UI passes alone.

The goal still requires correct authenticated account, agent, history and conversation; preserved /chat/messaging intent; every displayed provider; cancellation, expiry, replay, reload/BFCache, stale binding, reconnect and two contexts; explicit Dedicated price/consent; and no hidden identity/provisioning/lifecycle mutation. Dedicated must not become a prerequisite for Personal Shared. Three complete consecutive same-served-SHA cycles are still required.

#18627 owns fresh-account/running-agent/authenticated-Web-UI acceptance; its Google/same-account/logout receipts after #30884 remain valid. #29622 owns Dedicated/Personal Shared policy. No duplicate lane was opened. #30257 remains closed without merge; its unique local integration is preserved. The local code/media delivery did not invoke real provider, identity, database, deployment or lifecycle actions; the later resumed browser observation below has separate, explicitly limited provenance.

Public staging provenance checked on **8 September, 19:17 UTC**, without cookies or account requests: `staging.eliza.app` and `cloud-staging.eliza.app` serve renderer manifest source **e14071f00998f4d10f937015e3060196b991ad4d**, build ID `b8b603bfe07f79e26dee799710068dc961ca4b465393b2795b7b72fb4c103713`. This agrees with successful [staging release 34142406941](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/34142406941) for merged #30902. It verifies public metadata/root-document consistency, not all 503 asset bytes or authenticated behavior. At the resumed **21:18 UTC** read, the public renderer manifest still reports that same source/build. Our current PR head is not an ancestor of that served source, so this staging snapshot cannot qualify #30920. No deployment was attempted. The existing #18627 receipts remain scoped historical evidence, and owner PR #30915 was still open/unmerged at the earlier read.

The exact-head CI requirement is now satisfied: run **34265165075 completed successfully** at the 19:25 UTC read, including Source static smoke and All Tests Passed. Do not keep treating it as queued or restart that completed run. Before Ready, the still-missing whole-candidate independent verdict and applicable installed-platform/process-spanning and shared-consumer evidence must be resolved; these are not waived by green CI. The three complete live same-served-SHA cycles are a separate original-goal acceptance obligation, not a claim that this unmerged PR is already deployed.

**Resumed browser inspection — 8 September, 21:18 UTC: operator lock resolved.** The required in-app browser now works. From the real staging home, clicking only Sign in opened `/login?intent=launch`, then automatically reached `/join` without entering credentials or choosing a provider. This appears to resume an existing session; it does not prove a fresh login, correct account identity, or an authenticated agent/conversation. Current advertised login methods were not exposed by this path.

The real `/join` surface displays existing-Dedicated reuse, an error state, explicit hosting price, Cancel setup, Start Dedicated and Sign out. It fits both 1280×720 and a 390×844 narrow desktop viewport without horizontal page overflow. Narrow context has a fine pointer, so this is not installed-mobile or touch-target certification. With Tab, Cancel setup is focus-visible by DOM state but had no obvious visible focus treatment in the inspected screenshot; computed background was transparent with no border, shadow or painted outline. This bounded UX observation belongs to #29622, whose owner already has `JoinPage.tsx` in progress; no overlapping source edit or new PR was made. Account balance and private account-specific values are withheld, and the account-bearing screenshots are not uploaded.

No provider, Cancel setup, Start Dedicated or Sign out control was activated, and no credentials were entered. **This does not prove absence of automatic lifecycle requests:** browser/server request correlation was not obtained. The existing #29622 receipt [5576908511](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/29622#issuecomment-5576908511) reports a consent-bypassing automatic activation branch on this same served source. Visible consent is therefore not clearance of the whole route. Do not repeat entry, reload or cancellation as an assumed read-only test. Current server job/cost state remains unknown without applicable attested owner evidence.

**User-completed sign-out and provider inventory — 8 September, 21:32 UTC:** the user reports having signed out; the existing browser tab now visibly shows `/login`. The agent did not repeat logout, and did not collect server revocation receipts, so this is a user-reported action plus observed login landing, not a new end-to-end logout certification. The earlier request for logout authorization is superseded, not still a blocker.

The login page initially displayed the provider-discovery error and Retry sign-in options alongside cached-looking non-wallet controls. After inspecting the served source's bounded provider-list reload handler, one Retry click produced Loading sign-in options, then the error disappeared and Continue with a wallet appeared. Expanding only that disclosure exposed EVM and Solana; neither chain button was clicked. The actual visible inventory is phone/SMS, email Magic Link, Passkey and Use an existing passkey, Google, Discord, GitHub, X, Telegram, EVM and Solana. Telegram's widget was not opened. This establishes displayed methods and one successful UI recovery from discovery failure, not provider authentication or a verified network/root-cause diagnosis of the initial failure. No form value, provider control, wallet connection, credential/signature or grant was submitted. Public cloud-staging renderer metadata still reports the same e14071f source/build. Screenshots were inspected locally; no new media upload or installed-mobile certification.

Next action: reconcile a verified non-mutating entry path with #29622 before another actual login cycle, then obtain only the exact action-time provider/identity authority required for that step. The separate pre-Ready verdict/evidence requirements remain missing, and original acceptance is still 0/3. Browser tab3 remains on login for handoff; no temporary viewport override was added. No capture producer or hosted candidate job remains live; no new cache/worktree was created or deleted. Active non-ready work, dirty main, unique old integration and owner work remain protected.

### Execution handoff — 8 September, 21:52 UTC

The same external dependency is unchanged across three consecutive continuation checks after the successful browser/provider-inventory work. This is an execution impasse, not completed product acceptance: **0/3** remains. Fresh develop and clean pushed candidate are unchanged; staging still serves e14071f; no new owner or independent review receipt was returned. All applicable completed local producers and the exact-head CI are terminal. Repeating passed suites, creating more equivalent fixtures, or publishing repeated unchanged status would not satisfy the missing real-world requirements.

Concrete resumption conditions: #29622 supplies a served correction/verified entry contract that prevents unconfirmed lifecycle activation; #18627 supplies its remaining owned fresh-account/agent/Web-UI evidence; and #30920 obtains the outstanding independent verdict plus applicable installed-platform/process-spanning/shared-consumer qualification under the necessary specific operator authority. These are separate obligations, not a request to deploy or merge this draft. No review clearance is inferred from a tool failure and no refused investigation will be retried or routed around. Mac unlocking and user sign-out are already resolved and must not be requested again. Reconcile any new evidence on resumption before asking for a particular provider or device action. No pending push or additional safe cleanup was identified; all unique work remains preserved.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Integrates one shared session-authority coordinator through the actual SDK, network, canonical storage and UI consumers.
- Captures generation, token, target and cancellation lifetime; abandoned work cannot silently adopt new authority.
- Retires page-hidden background and SSO work; returning to SSO preserves the login destination without replaying consumed proofs.
- **Latest correction:** a legitimate concurrent renewal or selection change restarts restoration from fresh inputs, with a three-attempt bound, instead of painting a fatal agent-start error. Pagehide/unmount cancellation remains inert; pageshow resumes restoration; timeout, unavailable authority and exhausted churn retain visible recovery.
- Adds real-consumer regression tests with controlled HTTP/lock/native transports. No provider configuration, server migration or deployment change.

# Relates to

Relates to #30904 — fixes the JSON-escaped and literal-split paths in the constrained `ResponseSkeletonStreamExtractor` (`processActiveString` → `appendVisibleAndEmit`) that the issue reproduces. Kept as `Relates to` rather than `Closes` so #30904 stays open to track the pre-existing passthrough/prose-mode split: `drainPassthrough` (`streaming.ts:751`) emits its buffer verbatim, so a literal surrogate pair split across `push()` boundaries in passthrough mode is still delivered malformed. That path is explicitly scoped out here (see Risks) and is the same holdback shape applied to a different drain; flagged by @hermesagent270-commits' executed review at `ef9ca36` and left as a follow-up.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun install` was run; package `test`, `typecheck`, `lint`, and both build targets pass (see evidence). Full `bun run verify` not run on this ARM dev box — the change is scoped to one core module and its unit tests.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works from the failing→passing test output below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Based on latest `origin/develop` (`git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/develop` = 0 at push time); zero conflicts.
- [x] Focused package checks pass post-sync. Full `bun run verify` is a repo-wide gate; scoped verification is documented under Known gaps.

# Risks

Low. The change is confined to `ResponseSkeletonStreamExtractor.appendVisibleAndEmit` (chunk-boundary logic) plus a new end-of-stream `flushPendingSurrogate` step in `flush()`. Field routing, ordering, span parsing, reasoning-tag filtering, and passthrough mode are untouched. For any content with no lone surrogate at a chunk boundary the behavior is byte-identical (the ASCII/BMP control test proves this). The only observable change is that an emitted chunk is now always well-formed UTF-16: a trailing lone high surrogate is held back for its low half, and any other unpaired surrogate is replaced with U+FFFD.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`ResponseSkeletonStreamExtractor` (`packages/core/src/utils/streaming.ts`) is the per-token stream handed to clients (constructed in the model dispatcher, feeding `downstreamChunk` → `paramsChunk`/`ctxChunk`). It could deliver a chunk that is not well-formed UTF-16: a non-BMP code point (e.g. an emoji 😀) was split into its two UTF-16 surrogate code units emitted as two separate `onChunk` chunks. Two independent paths caused it:

1. **Escaped path** — when a provider serializes a non-BMP char as a JSON escape pair (`\uXXXX\uXXXX`), `processActiveString` decoded each `\uXXXX` escape independently and called `appendAndEmit` immediately, so the two halves emitted as separate chunks inside a single `push()`.
2. **Literal path** — the loop consumes one UTF-16 code unit at a time, so an unescaped emoji split whenever a `push()` boundary fell between its halves.

Clients encode each individual chunk into UTF-8 SSE frames / WebSocket text frames / `JSON.stringify`, all of which corrupt a lone surrogate.

**Fix:** both paths funnel through `appendVisibleAndEmit`, so the surrogate handling lives there once. When the chunk about to be emitted ends on a lone high surrogate, that code unit is held back and prepended to the next emission once its trailing low surrogate arrives. Any *interior* unpaired surrogate that remains in the releasable prefix — an interior lone high not followed by a low (`A\ud83dB`) or an isolated low (`A\ude00B`) — is replaced with U+FFFD via `toWellFormedUnicode` before emission; the replacement is 1:1 by code unit, so the length-based emission cursor stays valid. `emittedContent` therefore stays well-formed and is the running join of emitted chunks (also passed as the `accumulated` argument, which stays consistent and well-formed), and `fieldContents` mirrors the well-formed emitted value plus at most one still-raw pending high surrogate. At genuine end-of-stream, `flushPendingSurrogate` emits any still-held lone high surrogate as U+FFFD — matching the codebase's existing well-formed convention — rather than dropping a real character or shipping a lone surrogate.

This second sanitization step closes the P2 review finding ([`ss251`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/30919#pullrequestreview)): withholding only a *trailing* high surrogate left non-trailing unpaired surrogates reaching `onChunk` unchanged.

No character is lost or duplicated: joining all emitted chunks for a field reconstructs the original decoded string; only chunk boundaries within a field change so they never fall between surrogate halves.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation. Behavior of a public streaming utility is made correct (well-formed chunks) without changing its API.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/streaming-field-events.test.ts` — six regression tests in the `ResponseSkeletonStreamExtractor` describe block. They fail on `develop` and pass with this change.

## Detailed testing steps

```bash
cd packages/core
bun run test src/utils/__tests__/streaming-field-events.test.ts
```

Covered: escaped emoji `\ud83d\ude00` in a single `push()`; literal emoji split across two `push()` boundaries; a genuinely lone trailing high surrogate at `flush()` (→ U+FFFD); and an ASCII/BMP control that stays byte-identical and still streams incrementally. Each test asserts `c.isWellFormed()` for every emitted chunk and that `chunks.join("")` reconstructs the original string.

# Evidence Gate

<!-- evidence-head:ef9ca3681dc175ba2e765c796295e0711c021c03 -->


The two added tests (`replaces an interior lone high surrogate followed by more text`, `replaces an isolated low surrogate`) assert `isWellFormed()` on every emitted chunk **and** on the accumulated callback value, and that the lone unit is replaced by U+FFFD.
<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->

<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
